Additional hurdles include suboptimal choice of drug cargo, insufficient tumour targeting, and inadequate preclinical biological validation.

headline: Engineering tumor-specific interferon-alpha-Nivolumab pro-immunocytokine for enhanced melanoma immunotherapy
summary: Interferon-alpha (IFNα)-Nivolumab is a tumor-selective pro-immunocytokine. It combines IFNα signaling with PD-1 blockade. In a humanized ASID mouse melanoma model, it significantly reduced tumor volume. It also showed increased CD4+/CD8+ T cell infiltration and enhanced MHC I expression. headline: Rhino-orbito-cerebral mucormycosis in new-onset type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case-based short review
summary: Mucormycosis is an aggressive angioinvasive fungal infection that commonly involves the paranasal sinuses, orbit, lungs, and central nervous system. headline: ZebRack: A budget-friendly mobile system for short-term zebrafish housing
summary: ZebRack is an open-source, budget-friendly mobile zebrafish housing system. Built for under US$900, this modular 15-tank setup features 2.8-l tanks integrated into a compact framework. headline: Tibial Bone-Anchored Prostheses: A Narrative Review of the Literature and Reflection on 10 Years of Surgical Practice
summary: Historically, bone-anchored prosthesis (BAP) treatment was developed for the treatment of individuals with a transfemoral amputation. summary: Concrete production consumes nearly 16% of global freshwater resources. headline: Multileaf Faraday cup for beam energy verification in radiation therapy with ultra-high dose-rate electron beams and ion beams
summary: In radiotherapy and particle therapy, the stability of the beam energy must be checked routinely during quality assurance. This is of particular importance when varying the dose rate via the beam intensity of the accelerator to study the FLASH effect. A compact, portable multileaf Faraday cup (MLFC) with 128 channels was developed for energy determination based on the measurement of depth-charge curves. Its design is optimized for clinical electron beams in a range between 3 and 25 MeV.
evidence_points: Purpose: The standard method of energy verification based on the measurement of percent depth-dose curves in a water phantom is time-consuming and in the case of ultra-high dose-rate beams, may also present a non-negligible radiation protection problem.
Methods: A compact, portable multileaf Faraday cup (MLFC) with 128 channels was developed for energy determination based on the measurement of depth-charge curves.
Its design is optimized for clinical electron beams in a range between 3 and 25 MeV.
Changes in the beam energy of below 20 keV (0.1% of 20 MeV) can be clearly identified by means of the MLFC.
For proton beams, well-defined peaks in the depth-charge curves are observed for each single synchrotron spill with a total charge of only about 1 nC.
The energy values resulting from MC simulations of the measured MLFC data agree with the actual proton energies within 2 % $\%$ .
